messages:
Maya: FYI we got a request from BigTel to always route their traffic to our low-latency dedicated pool in us-west-2. They want an "always-pin" option and an auditable trail for compliance.

jorge: Do they mean sticky session -> single pool, or header-based pinning per org?

Maya: header-based. they'll set `x-corp-routing: bigtel` on requests. they want an override at org level that beats normal routing policies.

Linh: That header feels fine. we already accept `x-org-id` for tenant scoping. question is precedence: should per-org pin be a hard override or a preference with fallback?

Samir: For enterprise SLAs I think hard override makes sense, but we need fail-open behavior if the pool is down. i.e. fallback to best-effort hosted variants but mark request as "violated-pin" for billing/alerts.

Ava: +1. also we need an allowlist UI so only approved pools can be selected per-org. otherwise sales will ask for arbitrary pools and ops will be 😬 :eyes:  

Maya: proposal: add a new `org_routing_overrides` object in control-plane (editable in Console). fields: org_id, header_key, match_value, target_pool, mode=[strict|graceful], reason, owner, created_by. show audit entries in Console and emit `routing.override` events to telemetry.

jorge: how do we represent the rule in gateway config? something like: 
```
- match: headers['x-corp-routing'] == 'bigtel'
  route: dedicated/us-west-2/pool-42
  metadata: { org: 'bigtel', mode: 'strict', override_id: 'or-123' }
```

Samir: gateway needs to enforce precedence. we currently evaluate route rules by specificity score; org overrides should get +1000 priority so they always win unless in graceful mode and pool unavailable.

Linh: telemetry: tag requests with `routing.source=org_override` and `routing.override_id`. send counts to cost/latency dashboards and create a regression alert if lat > 2x baseline for that org.

Ava: security: restrict who can create overrides (enterprise admin + security review). also validate target_pool belongs to the same customer account or to our dedicated catalog; no cross-org leaks.

Maya: audit-bot will post an entry whenever an override is created/changed/deleted. sample message: 
"audit-bot: [or-123] override created by maya — org=bigtel target=dedicated/us-west-2/pool-42 mode=strict reason='compliance'"

jorge: edge case: what if multiple headers match (x-org-id + x-corp-routing) with different targets? need deterministic tie-breaker.

Samir: tie-breaker RFC: explicit override rule (org_routing_overrides) > tenant header `x-org-id` > weighted routing > default. also add `created_at` recency as final tie-breaker.

Linh: quotas: route pinning might concentrate traffic on small pools. recommend we enforce soft per-pool qps caps and surface quota exhaustion in Console (and allow buying capacity).

Ava: ops-bot: can we simulate an override in staging without touching prod routing? want the Console to have a "dry-run" toggle that flips telemetry to `org_override:dry` and doesn't change actual routing.

ops-bot: noted. adding `dry_run` on the API and a flag in gateway config that marks rule as inactive but emits telemetry.

Maya: Dev plan:
- API: POST /orgs/{org}/routing_overrides (create/read/list/delete)
- Console: UI for create + audit trail + dry-run toggle
- Control plane: validation + allowlist checks + emit audit events
- Gateway: priority + graceful fallback + telemetry tags

jorge: ETA? we should target a small canary with BigTel by EOW next week.

Samir: i'll prototype gateway priority change and graceful fallback this week. putting a PR up by Wed.

Linh: I'll wire telemetry and dashboards; need the schema for `routing.override` events.

Maya: I'll own Console mockups and the compliance checklist. tagging @Ava for RBAC rules.

Ava: Roger. i'll draft RBAC + approval flow and post the doc: https://go.redwood/ops/org-routing-policy (WIP).

Maya: thanks team. quick note: make sure we surface override usage in per-route cost breakdowns so finance can reconcile.

audit-bot: [or-123] created by Maya at 1842127897 — org=bigtel target=dedicated/us-west-2/pool-42 mode=strict

jorge: cool. follow-ups: add unit tests for precedence, and a migration to ensure existing header-only rules don't regress.

Samir: noted, will include tests in PR.

Maya: ok wrapping up. will DM BigTel the dry-run link once staging is up. :thumbsup:
